chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has ten shirts and rotates between them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to own and rotate multiple shirts according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that possessing and rotating ten shirts is permissible, addressing the specific concern of whether such quantity constitutes extravagance (*israf*) or mere necessity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that moderate accumulation of clothing for practical rotation is not inherently blameworthy, provided it does not cross into excessive luxury. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the boundaries of personal wealth management in daily life.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have ten shirts for him, rotating between these. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a man can have ten shirts, changing them every day. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not unlawful.’”
